item.title: 📹 Corinthians end 10-game winless run to ease pressure in bottom four
item.description: 📹 Corinthians end 10-game winless run to ease pressure in bottom four Corinthians beat Mirassol 2-0 at the Neo Química Arena on Friday (30) in Matchday 33 of the 2026 Brasileirão. Timão had not won a league game since their 2-0 victory over RB Bragantino on August 9 and were on a 10-match winless run. This was also the team's first win under Dutch coach Clarence Seedorf, following a 1-1 draw with Vitória and a 3-2 defeat to Vasco. ⚽ The match With the unwavering support of their faithful fans from the opening whistle, Corinthians completely dominated proceedings. However, the weight of their 10-match winless run affected the Corinthians players' decision-making, especially in the "final third." Things became easier, though, when the referee sent off Bruno Santos after a VAR review in the 23rd minute. With a one-man advantage, Timão created more chances and tried every kind of shot, but the game remained goalless at the break. As they headed to the dressing rooms, Mirassol's players and coach fiercely criticized the referee. After the restart, their dominance finally translated into goals. Playing as a left winger in Seedorf's system, Matheus Bidu popped up in the box like a center-forward to turn in Matheuzinho's cross and open the scoring 13 minutes into the second half. Then, in the 80th minute, Kaio César charged down the right, cut inside and curled a left-footed shot from the edge of the box beyond goalkeeper Walter to seal Corinthians' victory. 🚦 How things stand The result took Corinthians to 36 points and lifted them into 17th place, the highest of the four relegation spots, leaving Internacional third from bottom on 35 points. Mirassol remain on 37 points, just above the relegation zone. With five rounds remaining, five other clubs are still in serious danger of going down: Grêmio (37 points), Vitória (38 points), Vasco (38 points), Coritiba (39 points) and Botafogo (39 points). Coxa and Leão da Barra face each other on Saturday (31) to wrap up Matchday 33 of the Brasileirão. Vasco and Chapecoense also still have their postponed Matchday 21 fixture to play. The game is scheduled for November 14 at the Arena Condá. Mirassol are back in action as soon as next Tuesday (3), when they visit Chapecoense on Matchday 34. item.description: “I would never…”: Man United’s captain marvel Bryan Robson criticises Bruno Fernandes Bryan Robson has admitted that the Stretford End’s “STANDARDS” banner saddened him, while criticising Bruno Fernandes for questioning Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick in public. Fernandes dispute deepened United’s on-field crisis After United’s 4-1 defeat at Como on 21 October, Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned Carrick’s decision not to use a man-to-man press. The captain was then left as an unused substitute for the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth, during which supporters displayed the banner featuring Robson, Roy Keane and Eric Cantona. Carrick and Fernandes subsequently held clear-the-air talks at Carrington , with the Portugal international offering assurances over his commitment. Carrick has since confirmed that Fernandes will remain captain as United prepare to visit Chelsea. Robson says standards should not need explaining In an interview with The Daily Mail ), legendary captain Robson said players should understand the demands attached to representing United as soon as they arrive at the club. “Standards. The demand has always been to keep them high at Manchester United; you were aware the minute you walked through the door,” he said. The former captain said former manager Ron Atkinson had made those expectations clear to him, although he already knew what was required. Robson also stressed that the focus should be on hard work and United winning rather than the individual, adding “I would never have called out Sir Alex Ferguson in public.” Robson’s 13 years as a United player Robson joined United from West Bromwich Albion in 1981 for a British-record £1.5 million. He went on to make 461 appearances for the club and scored 99 goals. The midfielder won two league titles, three FA Cups and the European Cup Winners’ Cup during his time at Old Trafford. Injuries and the emergence of younger midfielders reduced his playing opportunities before he departed in 1994 to become Middlesbrough’s player-manager. Robson later managed Bradford City, West Bromwich Albion, Sheffield United and Thailand. He now serves as a United club representative. Final Thoughts Robson said the Stretford End’s “STANDARDS” banner made him sad. The former captain believes United players should already understand what the club demands. Robson said he would never have criticised former manager Sir Alex Ferguson publicly. Fernandes remains captain and is likely to return against Chelsea. item.title: Mark Walter Says ‘3 Ps’ Mean Dodgers Dynasty Will Continue
item.description: This week, Los Angeles Dodgers owner Mark Walter has sought to calm the fanbase after a sweep in the National League Championship Series brought LA’s three-peat hopes to an end. Speaking with Jack Harris of the California Post , Walter explained his philosophy when building the organization and detailed how, despite a tough end to this season, the Dodgers are set to compete for championships for years to come. What did Mark Walter say is the secret to the Dodgers’ success? Harris called an alliterative saying by Walter “the Dodgers’ guiding light.” “You’ve heard about the three strikes. But what about the 3 Ps?” Walter said. “Our people, our passion and our practice.” Oct 21, 2021; Los Angeles, California, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers chairman and controlling owner Mark Walter watches during game five of the 2021 NLCS against the Atlanta Braves at Dodger Stadium. The Dodgers defeated the Braves 11-2. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports Credit: USA TODAY Sports (Reuters) It’s hard to argue with the Dodgers’ recent success, as they’ve won three World Series titles since 2020. However, big changes are on the way. Not only is Walter facing a federal probe that preceded him selling off other teams like the Los Angeles Lakers — he promises he’s keeping the Dodgers — but a looming lockout could end with a salary cap in baseball. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Dodgers Nation (@dodgersnation) Much of the Dodgers’ recent success is often credited to their ability to sign high-end free agents and trade for superstars, but Walter said even with changes to the way teams must operate, the Dodgers are set up to succeed. “I think on any playing field, we’ll still be among the elite teams,” he said. “I think our people and our passion and our practice really does matter.” As evidence, he cites the Dodgers’ farm system, one of the best in the sport and a key, if often underrated, part of the team’s success. For instance, it was top prospect Josue De Paula who provided a spark at the end of this season, and it was another prospect, Zyhir Hope, who allowed the Dodgers to trade for ace Tarik Skubal . “It’s not just spending. Our farm system is pretty strong, and that and our player development are really big things for us.” President of baseball operations Andrew Friedman agreed with that assessment when speaking with Harris. “Just for us to have the farm system that we have, I think is something that gives all of us confidence in our ability to work together within whatever rules exist to be as good as we can possibly be,” he said. They went off right at 9," Pomperaug girls soccer coach Corrado Perugini said. "We knew it wasn't a power failure. The scoreboard was on. Everything else was still working." Perugini said the game started late, around 7:30 p.m. because the Newtown bus arrived late due to traffic. It took approximately 30 minutes to get the lights back on in full. Players were staying loose and then started to warm up again once the lights started to come back on. Neither could a first round of penalty kicks. No. 2 seed Pomperaug won in the second round of PKs 5-3 to advance to Sunday's SWC championship game against top seed Notre Dame Prep. The game will begin at 4 p.m. at Western Connecticut State University. Perugini noted that Pomperaug goalkeeper Madelyn Martino saved five consecutive PKs. "We have a great goalie," Perugini said. item.title: Brewers deliver the message that baseball is healthy. MLB owners should pay heed
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt celebrates after winning baseball's World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays, Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026, in St. Petersburg. (Ashley Landis/Associated Press) Major League Baseball owners have a big problem on their hands. They need to explain how the game is broken, and they don't have a shred of evidence. The recent postseason proved to be a blessed unveiling of common sense. For those fearing a lockout that could dismantle or even eliminate the 2027 season, the mighty Los Angeles Dodgers were sent home looking humbled and vulnerable. The other three semifinalists were veritable cheapskates at the marketplace, ranking 19th (Milwaukee Brewers), 28th (Tampa Bay Rays) and dead-last 30th (Cleveland Guardians) in payroll. Please, someone explain how this means disaster. Let's have the most hawkish owners, the ones planning to steer the negotiations of doomsday, come out of hiding for televised news conferences. "The owners" want this or that – sorry, that's far too vague. We need to see you in person, because baseball is absolutely thriving heading into winter. For my money, one of baseball's great things is the absence of a salary cap. The game operates on pure capitalism: Run your business correctly, with foresight, and reap the rewards. Bungle your way through the landscape, cutting corners at every turn, and pay the price. In fact, prepare to lose money at times. Just get better. And I really need to know how this system has hurt the game. The game's popularity was built on Yankees bombast, dating to Babe Ruth's time, larger-than-life clubs who spent big money but, more importantly, played the game at an ethereal level. – right through Derek Jeter's time. But it didn't have to be that way. One of the game's most memorable dynasties, the Oakland A's of 1972-74, were built on scotch tape and shoestrings. While owner Charlie Finley spent approximately no money (until the free-agent system drove him nuts), the team drafted and traded superbly, resulting in one of the most pristine baseball showcases – pitching, defense, power, speed, fundamental smarts – the sport has ever seen. item.title: Auburn’s Path to Bowl Game Clear but Steep
item.description: Oct 24, 2026; Auburn, Alabama, USA; Auburns mascot Aubie the Tiger greets fans at tiger walk prior to the game against the LSU Tigers at Jordan-Hare Stadium. Mandatory Credit: John Reed-Imagn Images Auburn football lost big to LSU last week, but the season is far from over. The Tigers’ path forward is clear, but very difficult. They need to win the rest of their November games to hit nine wins for the first time since 2019. Experts across the country believe the team can pull this off despite the recent loss. The path is hard, but the math is simple. USA TODAY Sports sticks with a Birmingham Bowl projection featuring Auburn against Memphis for the third week in a row. Memphis leads the all-time series, yet Auburn won the last meeting in that same bowl back in 2015. Erick Smith of USA TODAY Sports says the Tigers will play close to home again. This is a realistic goal if the team handles its upcoming opponents. Three games define the season Auburn plays a brutal schedule before the final stretch. The team faces Ole Miss on Saturday in what could be the toughest test of the month. If the Tigers win that road game, the rest of the schedule looks much more manageable. They then play three teams they should beat: Arkansas, Mississippi State, and Samford. Finally, they end the regular season on the road facing their in-state rivals, Alabama at Tuscaloosa. Winning out is the only way to reach the nine-win mark. ESPN’s Kyle Bonagura projects a matchup with USF in the Gasparilla Bowl if the team keeps winning. Another ESPN expert, Mark Schlabach, has tweaked his pick to put Auburn against Illinois in the Birmingham Bowl. CBS Sports analyst Brad Crawford also sees a trip to Birmingham, but he predicts a game against Boston College on December 29. That would be the first time since 2014 that Auburn has faced an ACC team in a postseason game. The experts see a winnable path Athlon Sports has changed its tune after predicting an Independence Bowl game last week . In the Birmingham Bowl, Steven Lassan now predicts Auburn will meet NC State. NC State fired its head coach and has a shaky record, but the Wolfpack can still find new life. ESPN predicts the team will win two of its final five games to get there. On3’s Brett McMurphy sees a different destination, pitting Auburn against Houston in the Liberty Bowl. The consensus is clear: Auburn can make a bowl if they stop the bleeding. The team lost 38-17 at home to a top-20 LSU squad. That loss hurts, but it does not end the season. The schedule in November offers a clear shot at redemption. Fans should watch the Ole Miss game closely, because that result will decide everything. If the Tigers win that one, the rest of the path opens up for a nine-win finish.
